cards.explanation: The answer is the Book of the Law. The people ask Ezra to bring out the Book of the Law of Moses, "…which the LORD had commanded for Israel." They're asking for the Book, friends, and I love that for them.

The answer is from daybreak until noon. Ezra read it aloud from sunrise to midday while facing the square (Nehemiah 8:3). That's hours and hours, friends. I once got tired just stamping one tray, so I'm impressed.
The answer is False. The text says "…all the people listened attentively to the Book of the Law." That's every single person, for hours, friends.

The answer is stand up! Ezra opens the book in full view of everyone, and "…all the people stood up." The moment the Book opens, the whole square is on its feet. That's a crowd that knows what's in front of them.

The answer is True! After their "Amen, Amen!" the people bowed down and worshiped the LORD "…with their faces to the ground." Hands lifted first, then faces down low. The whole square worships in a big way.

The answer is explained. They read from the Book of the Law of God, "…explaining it and giving insight, so that the people could understand what was being read." Reading is one thing, but they made sure it landed. Every good teacher wants that, and I sure do.

The answer is True. The text says "…all the people were weeping as they heard the words of the Law." It's the whole crowd, not just a few. I think that's a heavy moment, and the text lets it be heavy.
The answer is False. Nehemiah says, "Go and eat what is rich, drink what is sweet, and send out portions to those who have nothing prepared…" He sends them to the table, not away from it.

The answer is portions! Nehemiah says to "…send out portions to those who have nothing prepared…" He puts that right alongside the eating and drinking. So the feast comes with a gift for people who have nothing prepared.
The answer is the joy of the LORD. Nehemiah says, "Do not grieve, for the joy of the LORD is your strength." The strength he names is the joy of the LORD.

The answer is that they understood the words made known to them. The people began to eat and drink, to send out portions, and to rejoice greatly, "…because they understood the words that had been made known to them." The Levites explained it, and then the people understood. I love how much joy comes from that.

The answer is to study the words of the Law. On the second day, the heads of all the families, along with the priests and Levites, gather around Ezra "…to study the words of the Law." After a morning of listening, they come back for more. That's the kind of leaders I want.

The answer is branches! The message says, "Go out to the hill country and bring back branches of olive, wild olive, myrtle, palm, and other leafy trees, to make booths, as it is written." Those are the materials, straight from the hill country. That's the whole shopping list, friends, and it's all leaves.

The answer is False. The text says the people made booths "…on their own rooftops, in their courtyards, in the courts of the house of God, and in the squares by the Water Gate and by the Gate of Ephraim." The courts of the house of God are only one of those places. Booths went up on rooftops, in courtyards and in the squares too.

The answer is since the days of Joshua son of Nun. The text says, "From the days of Joshua son of Nun until that day, the Israelites had not celebrated like this." Joshua led Israel after Moses (Joshua 1:1-2). That's a very long stretch without a celebration like this one.

The answer is every day of the feast! The text says, "Day after day, from the first day to the last, Ezra read from the Book of the Law of God." The feast was seven days long. The reading went right along with it, from the first day to the last.

The answer is the eighth day. The text says the Israelites kept the feast for seven days, "…and on the eighth day they held an assembly, according to the ordinance." That's one more gathering right after the feast. I never mind a bonus day when it comes with good company.
